AnrlSqtpOkw.title: Alan Kay's tribute to Ted Nelson at "Intertwingled" Festival
AnrlSqtpOkw.summary: Alan Kay's tribute to Ted Nelson at the Intertwingled festival, presented using a revived Smalltalk-78 system running on emulated 1970s Xerox PARC hardware. It shows live, user-programmable software from that era.
AnrlSqtpOkw.why: HN returns to it again and again as a demonstration of how programmable and composable 1970s systems were compared with today's.

quote.text: a great example of what's not-even-close to possible on today's systems

gNRnrn5DE58.title: Origins of Precision
gNRnrn5DE58.summary: Machine Thinking traces where mechanical precision comes from, from flat surface plates and the three-plate method up through lathes and early measuring tools. It is the first in a series on recreating the first micrometer.
gNRnrn5DE58.why: HN commenters repeatedly recommend it as a half-hour mini-documentary on how precision is bootstrapped from scratch, relevant to machining and chip manufacturing threads.

quote.text: The Origins of Precision" is a half hour well spent

Mfsnlbd-4xQ.title: Functional Composition - Chris Ford
Mfsnlbd-4xQ.summary: Chris Ford builds up from a single sine wave through layered abstractions to a Bach canon, using Clojure and the Overtone audio environment. The talk shows music theory as a natural fit for functional programming.
Mfsnlbd-4xQ.why: HN repeatedly recommends it as a delightful talk that makes music theory click and introduces Clojure and Overtone.

quote.text: Recommend this talk that made Music 'click' for me.

vvZA9n3e5pc.title: Stanford Seminar - The Soul of a New Machine: Rethinking the Computer
vvZA9n3e5pc.summary: Bryan Cantrill of Oxide Computer Company gives a Stanford EE380 talk on rethinking the server. He argues that hyperscaler-style rack-scale machines with open firmware, RISC-V and Rust should be available to everyone, not just the giants.
vvZA9n3e5pc.why: HN points to it as the founders' own explanation of what Oxide is building and why, a frequent link whenever Oxide comes up.

categories.name: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages

quote.text: The talk lays out a history of servers, describes the problems with the servers that you can buy from vendors today

rvskMHn0sqQ.title: A Selfish Argument for Making the World a Better Place – Egoistic Altruism
rvskMHn0sqQ.summary: Kurzgesagt makes a selfish case for improving the world, arguing that helping people far away raises prosperity and innovation for everyone, including yourself. The animated video frames this as egoistic altruism and positive-sum cooperation.
rvskMHn0sqQ.why: HN commenters link it to argue for cooperation and engagement over isolation, and as an accessible statement of positive-sum thinking.

quote.text: There is a video [0] I love that explains an argument for this well.

j5v8D-alAKE.title: This is why we can't have nice things
j5v8D-alAKE.summary: Veritasium explores planned obsolescence, from the Phoebus lightbulb cartel to printers and phones. It explains how companies deliberately shortened product lifetimes and why products aren't better.
j5v8D-alAKE.why: Commenters link it as the engaging go-to explainer on planned obsolescence and the lightbulb cartel.

quote.text: Veritasium made a video that reviews the history and presents the topic in an engaging way.

k1BneeJTDcU.title: Welcome to the Internet - Bo Burnham (from "Inside" -- ALBUM OUT NOW)
k1BneeJTDcU.summary: Bo Burnham's song from his special Inside, a satirical take on internet culture, attention and extremism.
k1BneeJTDcU.why: HN commenters bring it up in threads about the internet, attention economy and smartphones, mostly as a favorite, with a few dissenters.

quote.text: This is one of my favourite songs now

s_osQvkeNRM.title: Stephen Fry on the Joys of Swearing
s_osQvkeNRM.summary: A short clip of Stephen Fry defending swearing as a rich and essential part of the English language and rejecting the idea that it is unnecessary.
s_osQvkeNRM.why: HN commenters post it in swearing and profanity debates as the best statement against taking offense at profanity.

5guXaWwQpe4.title: "Energy Revolution? More like a Crawl" - Dr. Vaclav Smil
5guXaWwQpe4.channel: Trottier Institute for Sustainability in Engineering and Design
5guXaWwQpe4.summary: Energy scholar Vaclav Smil argues that global energy transitions are slow and that renewable targets should not rest on wishful thinking. He appraises how energy dependencies are likely to change and asks for using much less.
5guXaWwQpe4.why: HN recommends it as a grounded, data-driven counter to hype about quick energy revolutions.

quote.text: I really suggest watching this talk by Smil

czgOWmtGVGs.title: A New History for Humanity – The Human Era
czgOWmtGVGs.summary: Kurzgesagt explains the Holocene or Human Era calendar, which adds 10,000 years to the current year to anchor dates to the start of human civilization. It argues this gives a more sensible frame for human history.
czgOWmtGVGs.why: Linked whenever year numbering or the Holocene calendar comes up as the accessible introduction to the idea.

quote.text: Kurtzgesagt has a really great video about the subject

9q3uNcJh4pc.title: Tiny meteorites are everywhere. Here’s how to find them.
9q3uNcJh4pc.summary: Verge Science's pilot of its Trial & Error series follows amateur scientist Jon Larsen on a hunt for micrometeorites. It shows how tiny space rocks can be found on rooftops and confirmed under a microscope.
9q3uNcJh4pc.why: HN recommends it as an accessible demonstration of how anyone can collect micrometeorites at home.

quote.text: Here's a good video running through one way to do this at home

FaAZAII2x0w.title: ONS 2015: Wednesday Keynote - Amin Vahdat
FaAZAII2x0w.summary: Google's Amin Vahdat gives the ONS 2015 keynote on Google's datacenter networking, including its custom hardware, software-defined networking and very high bisection bandwidth.
FaAZAII2x0w.why: HN cites it as a rare public look at Google's internal network design and how it scales to many VMs.

quote.text: If you're interested in datacenter networking, can't miss ONS.

ubDMLoWz76U.title: NixOS VM on Mac Setup
ubDMLoWz76U.summary: Mitchell Hashimoto walks through his setup for running a NixOS virtual machine on a Mac as his development environment, with a config repo on GitHub.
ubDMLoWz76U.why: HN points to it as a practical reference for the Linux-VM-on-Mac workflow and as an entry point to NixOS.

quote.text: My general setup mirrors this[1] pretty closely

w8c_m6U1f9o.title: The Power Of Selling Out: Your Customers As Political Capital - Onion Talks - Ep. 9
w8c_m6U1f9o.summary: A satirical Onion Talks episode in which a startup founder explains making money by selling his users' data to oppressive governments. It parodies tech conference talks and monetization of communities.
w8c_m6U1f9o.why: Posted as a joke or satire whenever a company sells out its users or surveillance comes up.

quote.text: This Onion talk put it really well

I25UeVXrEHQ.title: Richard Stallman Eats Something From His Foot
I25UeVXrEHQ.summary: A short clip from a lecture Q&A in which Richard Stallman appears to pick something off his foot and eat it.
I25UeVXrEHQ.why: Used as a recurring gag or jab at Stallman's social eccentricities; not recommended for its content.

PH1BKPSGcxQ.title: Chain of Fools 2017 - Every windows version upgraded through
PH1BKPSGcxQ.summary: TheRasteri upgrades a single PC through every Windows version, from early releases through Windows 10, testing that old software keeps running. It is an updated version of the Chain of Fools experiment.
PH1BKPSGcxQ.why: HN cites it as a demonstration of Windows' long backwards compatibility.
